We build low-latency query and serving layers on engines such as Apache Druid, ClickHouse and Apache Pinot, and extend them where our workload outgrows what they do out of the box. We write optimization and decision engines that replace work people were doing by hand. We build APIs that other services depend on, and the React web applications that operators and planners run their day from. And we build agentic systems on top of all of it, so a problem gets diagnosed and resolved by software rather than escalated to a human with a chart attached.
  
  
The work is operationally real. Our consumers are live systems, and ours matter most at exactly the moments something else is going wrong, so availability is a design constraint here rather than something handled after launch.

* Build real-time detection and alerting that tells an operator what changed and why it matters, rather than requiring them to know what to look for first
* Build rules and decision engines that replace large-scale manual workflows with software
* Build optimization systems that return the best available answer within a fixed time budget, degrading to a simpler strategy rather than failing
* Build and extend the APIs other services depend on, and the React web applications our operators and planners work in

Your closest collaborators are the engineers and scientists who build the forecasting and optimization models next to you — they need what your systems produce, and what they produce has to land in systems you operate.
